newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS PROMISED FAST TRACK.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS PROMISED FAST TRACK.

text.p: The Olympic Stadium in Athens will have a new, fast track for the world athletics championships next August.
The surface, costing between $700,000 and $1 million, will be similar to the one used at the Atlanta Olympics, where two world records fell in the men's sprints.
But long distance runners could face problems like those experienced in Atlanta.
Ethiopia's Haile Gebreselassie, the 10,000 metres gold medallist, blamed the hard track for injured feet which ruled him out of the 5,000 metres.
